sentences.text:
3. Heard the learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the second respondent, who is the de facto complainant and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.
4.

When the matters are taken up for hearing today, the learned counsel for the applicants as well as the learned counsel for the second respondent - de facto complainant would submit that both the parties have entered into compromise and they have amicably settled all the disputes between them and they have decided to compound the offence.
The learned counsel for the second respondent has also filed the affidavits of the second respondent - de facto complainant in both the cases to this effect.

It is stated in the affidavits by her that at the intervention of their family members that they have settled NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7358/2019 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined all the disputes amicably and that she has no grievance against the present applicants and that, she has no objection to quash the FIR.
5. The de facto complainant is physically present before the Court today.

When questioned, she has unequivocally stated that she has entered into compromise with the applicants, who are accused in the above crime and that, they have decided to compound the offence and that, she has no objection to quash the FIR.

6. Although, the offences for which the FIR was registered are of non-compoundable offences, as per the dictum laid down by the Apex Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, in appropriate cases, where the offences have not impact on the society, the Court, in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (CrPC), can permit the parties to compound the offences even which are non- compoundable.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though, the Apex Court has enlisted certain offences which cannot be permitted to be compounded, in the said judgment of the Apex Court, the present case is not falling within the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/7358/2019 ORDER DATED: 15/02/2024 undefined said exempted cases.
7. Therefore, permission is accorded to the applicants and the de facto complainant to compound the offence as prayed for and the compromise is recorded.

The FIR in Crime No. No. I-61 of 2019, registered with Adajan Police Station, Surat for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506(2) and 114 of the IPC, registered against the present applicants and the criminal proceedings initiated thereon, are hereby quashed.
